slides.headline: Tipasa Served Rome. Conquest Unmade It.
slides.subheadline: Trace a trading post’s transformation into Rome’s foothold, then ruins sustaining modern tourism.

items.label: DESTRUCTION
items.body: Vandal conquest destroyed ancient Tipasa.

items.label: REFOUNDATION
items.body: Modern Tipaza began anew; its ancient ruins now underpin tourism.

slides.svgBlueprint: Use a 1080×1350 viewBox with 80px margins. Paper #FFFFFF, Ink #000000, Accent #E60000, Surface #F5F5F5. Set publication masthead above a thin black rule; kicker in a red badge. Set the headline at 72px across three manually broken lines, subheadline at 30px. Place one abstract broken column behind the lower whitespace. Align two unboxed metric labels above the issue footer. No diagrams or callout boxes.

slides.headline: Rome Turned Trade Into A Foothold
slides.subheadline: Claudius converted a Punic trading post into a military colony for conquest.

items.label: LATER URBAN SCALE
items.body: Stéphane Gsell places Colonia Aelia Tipasensis at this population in the fourth century.

items.label: THE FUTURE RUPTURE
items.body: The colony’s imperial trajectory would end in Vandal destruction.

slides.svgBlueprint: Use 1080×1350, 80px margins, white ground and black typography. Set headline at 58px and subheadline at 30px. Build two broad ascending terraces, labeled PUNIC TRADE and ROMAN MILITARY COLONY; connect them with one red directional stroke. Attach each supplied metric and body to a terrace footer, explicitly retaining LATER and FUTURE labels. Use pale-gray terrace fills; avoid maps implying undocumented borders.

slides.kicker: THE HIDDEN DYNAMIC / MORE THAN A GARRISON
slides.headline: The Foothold Became A Christian Hub
slides.subheadline: Military origins gave way to a substantial city and an important religious centre.

items.label: FOURTH-CENTURY CITY
items.body: Stéphane Gsell’s population estimate reveals the scale behind the surviving ruins.

items.label: CHRISTIAN CENTRE
items.body: Christian institutions flourished during the last centuries of Roman governorship.

slides.svgBlueprint: Use 1080×1350 with white background and 80px margins. Place the 58px headline above a monumental 96px population numeral; keep inhabitants directly beneath at 30px. Add the attribution body at 28px. Reserve the lower third for one pale-gray basilica card with a red three-arch emblem, exact badge wording and body. Treat the arches as symbolic, not reconstructed architectural evidence.

slides.headline: Then The Vandals Broke The City
slides.subheadline: An established Christian hub met a conquest that destroyed its urban fabric.

items.label: THE ESTABLISHED CITY
items.body: Tipasa had become an important Christian hub under Roman governorship.

items.label: THE RUPTURE
items.body: The Vandals destroyed Tipasa.

slides.svgBlueprint: Use 1080×1350. Keep a white header with 58px headline and 30px subheadline. Below, divide the canvas into a white left field and black right field with a narrow red seam. Place the basilica item left in black and the destruction item right in white. Use 42px badges and 28px bodies. Interrupt a single horizontal architectural baseline at the seam; show no invented battle movements.

slides.headline: Destruction Was Not Yet The End
slides.subheadline: Byzantine reconstruction reopened the city’s story after the Vandal rupture.

items.label: CITY DESTROYED
items.body: Vandal conquest broke the Roman-era city.

items.label: CITY RECONSTRUCTED
items.body: The Byzantines reconstructed Tipasa, reversing destruction without securing permanent survival.

slides.svgBlueprint: Use 1080×1350, white background and 80px margins. Set a 58px headline above a thin black vertical spine containing exactly two milestone nodes. At the first, interrupt the line with a red gap; at the second, resume it in black. Place 40px badges and 28px bodies to the right. Behind the second node, use a pale-gray outline of reassembled blocks, explicitly schematic rather than archaeological.

slides.headline: Rebuilt, Then Reduced To Ruins Again
slides.subheadline: Umayyad demolition ended the reconstructed city’s reprieve, leaving ruins rather than continuity.

items.label: AFTER THE 430 CE DESTRUCTION
items.body: Byzantine reconstruction had restored the city after its earlier destruction.

items.badge: the end of the seventh century
items.label: UMAYYAD DEMOLITION
items.body: Umayyad forces demolished Tipasa and reduced it to ruins.

slides.svgBlueprint: Use 1080×1350 with a 58px headline and 30px subheadline. Place a small pale-gray reconstruction card above a larger white demolition card outlined in black. Use one red horizontal cut through a symbolic block silhouette between them. Set the long demolition badge at 34px over three lines without shortening its wording. Keep bodies at 28px and generous separation between the two cards.

slides.kicker: THE RIPPLE / A BROKEN URBAN SEQUENCE
slides.headline: The Next Chapter Took Centuries
slides.subheadline: Resettlement came much later, breaking any simple story of uninterrupted urban survival.

items.badge: the end of the seventh century
items.label: DEMOLITION
items.body: The ancient city was reduced to ruins.

items.label: RESETTLEMENT
items.body: The location was settled again, long after the ancient city’s destruction.

slides.svgBlueprint: Use 1080×1350 with white ground. Put the 58px headline and 30px subheadline in the top quarter. Position two 32px date badges near the upper and lower ends of a broken vertical spine. Leave the centre conspicuously empty, crossed only by a short red discontinuity mark. Keep each 28px body beside its node. Do not scale the gap numerically or imply verified total absence of inhabitants.

slides.kicker: THE DILEMMA / INHERITANCE IS NOT CONTINUITY
slides.headline: Same Place. Not An Unbroken City.
slides.subheadline: The interpretive trap: shared geography can conceal destruction, reconstruction and a later foundation.

items.label: ANCIENT TIPASA
items.body: Stéphane Gsell places the Roman-era city at this population in the fourth century.

items.label: MODERN TIPAZA
items.body: The modern town’s foundation belongs to a distinct, much later chapter.

slides.svgBlueprint: Use 1080×1350, white background, 80px margins and 58px headline. Below the subheadline, set TIPASA and TIPAZA as large opposing nameplates in two tall columns. Highlight only their differing letters in red. Place one metric and body beneath each name, using pale-gray backing on the modern side. Separate columns with a broken black rule; do not draw an arrow suggesting uninterrupted succession.

slides.kicker: THE DECISIVE THRESHOLD / A NEW FOUNDATION
slides.headline: 1857 Resets The City’s Clock
slides.subheadline: Resettlement becomes a modern town with its own foundation date.

items.label: RETURN TO THE SITE
items.body: Settlement resumed at the location of ancient Tipasa.

items.label: MODERN FOUNDATION
items.body: Tipaza’s foundation marks a new urban chapter, not uninterrupted ancient survival.

slides.svgBlueprint: Use 1080×1350 with white background and black typography. Place the headline at 58px, then make 1857 the central 160px red numeral. Attach its label and 28px body directly beneath. Place the nineteenth-century item in one shallow pale-gray footer card with a 34px badge. Use a black baseline under the hero date to suggest a new foundation, not a fabricated deadline.

slides.kicker: THE VERDICT / RUINS BECOME THE DRAW
slides.headline: Conquest Left Ruins. Tourism Found Value.
slides.subheadline: Can a city inherit an empire’s remains without inheriting its continuity?

items.label: DESTRUCTION IN THE RECORD
items.body: Vandal destruction was followed by Byzantine reconstruction and later Umayyad demolition.

items.label: A DIFFERENT CITY’S INHERITANCE
items.body: Founded in 1857, modern Tipaza owes its tourism importance chiefly to the ancient ruins.
